summary: The sample implements a working Python RAG demo that stores chunked patient records with embeddings, prefilters by patientId, re-ranks candidates in-application using cosine similarity, constructs a structured clinical-summary prompt, and returns grounded answers with document references. Unit tests run locally and mock external services. Major gaps are: no DB-side vector index is created (the builder intentionally used an application-side rerank fallback because authoritative index-creation docs were not available in the run), no provider-side $search/knn usage, limited retry/429 handling, and a few missing documentation/IaC pieces the gallery expects. Note: this run had no external documentation search available, so many of the discovered-practice entries come from files in the repository rather than public docs.

requirement_results.requirement: A Python RAG agent built with LlamaIndex answers a clinical question about a patient: one agent retrieves relevant record sections from Azure DocumentDB and produces the summary from them.
requirement_results.evidence: app/main.py (lines 41-48) implements /search that retrieves patient chunks and calls summarizer; README references LlamaIndex as an integration point (README.md lines 40-45), but no llama_index import or usage appears in code.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Add minimal LlamaIndex usage in the summarization pipeline (e.g., import llama_index and wrap prompt/context as an LlamaIndex query flow) or remove LlamaIndex from README and update requirement to document the integration path.

requirement_results.requirement: Patient records are split into chunks and each chunk is stored as a document in Azure DocumentDB with its embedding on the document, written through LlamaIndex's vector store integration or a MongoDB-compatible Python driver (e.g. pymongo).
requirement_results.evidence: seed.py lines 16-24 create chunk documents with 'embedding' field; app/app/store.py lines 15-21 upserts documents via pymongo.

requirement_results.requirement: Every stored patient-record document carries a `patientId` field.
requirement_results.evidence: seed.py lines 18-21 set 'patientId' on each chunk; queries filter by patientId in app/app/store.py line 36.

requirement_results.requirement: A cosmosSearch vector index (kind vector-ivf, vector-hnsw or vector-diskann) is created in code on the embedding field, with `dimensions` matching the embedding model the app uses.
requirement_results.evidence: No DB-side vector index creation code found. app/app/store.py.ensure_indexes (lines 11-13) creates only a patientId index; seed.py does not create a kNN/vector index.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Add idempotent, validated index-creation code to the seed script (e.g., a createIndex call that uses a variable EMBEDDING_DIM) and document it in README; prefer shipping a validated snippet in the agent-kit so builders don't guess provider-specific option names.

requirement_results.requirement: Retrieval embeds the clinical question and runs the similarity search in Azure DocumentDB with `$search` / `cosmosSearch` (similarity COS, L2 or IP).
requirement_results.evidence: The app computes an embedding (app/app/embeddings.py) then prefilters by patientId and re-ranks candidate embeddings in-application (app/app/store.py lines 34-56). No `$search` / cosmosSearch usage in code.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Implement a DB-side $search/knn attempt with fallback: try the provider-specific $search/knn aggregation (guarded by a feature-detection step) and fall back to the existing application-side re-rank if it is not supported.

requirement_results.requirement: Retrieval is limited to the requested patient's records by `patientId`, so sections of other patients are never retrieved (e.g. a `filter` on `patientId` inside `cosmosSearch`).
requirement_results.evidence: app/app/store.py.query_by_patient_and_rerank uses collection.find({"patientId": patient_id}, ...) to prefilter candidates (line 36).

requirement_results.requirement: The summarization prompt is assembled deliberately (context engineering): instructions for a clinical summary, the retrieved sections as context and the clinical question are placed in a structured layout.
requirement_results.evidence: app/app/summarizer.py PROMPT_TEMPLATE (lines 12-20) assembles Question and Context sections; summarize formats context blocks including doc and chunk ids (lines 26-29).

requirement_results.requirement: The answer is grounded in the retrieved sections and returned together with references to the source documents it drew on.
requirement_results.evidence: summarizer includes doc/chunk ids in the prompt (app/app/summarizer.py lines 26-29); app/main.py returns the retrieved sources along with the answer (app/app/main.py lines 47-49).

requirement_results.requirement: The connection string and model credentials come from environment variables; none appear in the repository.
requirement_results.evidence: app/app/db.py reads DOCUMENTDB_URI from the environment (lines 8-11); app/app/embeddings.py reads OPENAI_API_KEY from the environment (line 21). .env.example contains placeholders.

requirement_results.requirement: A `.env.example` lists every setting with placeholder values.
requirement_results.evidence: app/.env.example lists DOCUMENTDB_URI and OPENAI_API_KEY (app/.env.example).
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Add any optional or used env vars to .env.example (for example OPENAI_CHAT_MODEL, and note EMBEDDING_DIM if user should align index dimensions).

requirement_results.requirement: The vector index dimensions match the embedding model's output.
requirement_results.evidence: app/app/embeddings.py defines EMBEDDING_DIM = 1536 (line 4). No DB-side vector index is created so index dimensions are not applied in the DB.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: When adding DB-side index creation, reference EMBEDDING_DIM and use it when creating the vector index so dimensions are consistent.

requirement_results.requirement: The vector index parameters are chosen for the sample's data size, and the README says how to change them for a larger one.
requirement_results.evidence: No provider-side vector index exists in seed.py or anywhere; README (app/README.md lines 43-45) only notes the fallback and suggests how to add a native index at a high level but provides no tuned parameter defaults.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Add example index parameter defaults in the README and in seed.py (document initialCapacity/efConstruction/efSearch or IVF params) and describe how to change them for larger datasets.

requirement_results.requirement: One database client is created and reused across requests.
requirement_results.evidence: app/app/main.py implements a lazy singleton get_store() that creates a DocumentStore once and reuses it (lines 11-15). DocumentStore stores the collection (app/app/store.py lines 7-9) which was created via get_collection/get_db/get_client at construction time (app/app/db.py lines 20-27).

requirement_results.requirement: A seed script loads sample data and creates the index, and can be run twice without duplicating data.
requirement_results.evidence: seed.py uses deterministic _id values (lines 15, 17-25) and DocumentStore.upsert_chunks uses replace_one with upsert=True when _id present (app/app/store.py lines 15-21), making seeding idempotent. seed.py calls store.ensure_indexes() but does not create a DB-side vector index.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Make index creation in seed.py idempotent for vector index as well (wrap createIndex in try/except or check index_information), using deterministic names/parameters.

requirement_results.requirement: /search returns a clear error for an empty query and when the embedding call fails.
requirement_results.evidence: app/app/main.py raises HTTP 400 if patientId or question are empty (lines 42-44). The code does not catch exceptions from the embedding provider call, so embedding-call failures would surface as 500s without a clear diagnostic.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Wrap embedding calls with try/except in the /search handler and return a clear 5xx/4xx error with a helpful message when embedding fails (and include brief guidance about OPENAI_API_KEY or network errors).

requirement_results.requirement: Search results include the similarity score.
requirement_results.evidence: DocumentStore returns 'score' in each result (app/app/store.py lines 51-56) and /search returns the sources list (app/app/main.py line 49).

requirement_results.requirement: Dependencies are pinned in `requirements.txt`.
requirement_results.evidence: requirements.txt pins specific versions (e.g. pymongo==4.6.1, fastapi==0.95.2).

requirement_results.requirement: Unit tests run without a live cluster.
requirement_results.evidence: tests/test_app.py monkeypatches the store to a DummyStore and tests passed (events.jsonl shows '3 passed, 1 skipped').

requirement_results.requirement: Infrastructure for the cluster is provided as code, using the Azure DocumentDB resource type.
requirement_results.evidence: No IaC (Bicep/ARM/Terraform) files are present in the repository to provision an Azure DocumentDB/mongodbClusters resource.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Add an example IaC snippet (Bicep/Terraform azapi resource) and a short note in README showing the exact resource type and minimal parameters; include it as an optional folder (infra/) that is clearly marked 'manual/optional'.

requirement_results.requirement: The README covers what the sample shows, prerequisites, setup, run, and clean-up.
requirement_results.evidence: app/README.md includes Overview, Prerequisites, Quickstart, and Cleaning up (lines 1-36, 51-52).

requirement_results.requirement: The sample uses the name "Azure DocumentDB" throughout, and no former or neighbouring product name.
requirement_results.evidence: README and skill.md state 'Azure DocumentDB' and explicitly warn about similarly named neighbours (README.md lines 5-6 and run-environment notes).

checks.practice: Load the DocumentDB connection string from an environment variable (DOCUMENTDB_URI) and do not hard-code credentials in source control; provide a .env.example with a placeholder instead.
checks.evidence: app/app/db.py lines 8-11; app/.env.example

checks.practice: Create an index on patientId to enable efficient server-side filtering by patient before any re-ranking or context assembly.
checks.evidence: app/app/store.py.ensure_indexes creates index on ('patientId', 1) (lines 11-13); seed.py calls store.ensure_indexes() (lines 30-31).

checks.practice: Store embeddings as an array field on each chunk document alongside explicit metadata fields such as patientId, source_doc_id, chunk_id and created_at.
checks.evidence: seed.py lines 17-24 build documents with fields 'patientId','source_doc_id','chunk_id','text','embedding','metadata', and upsert persists them (app/app/store.py lines 15-21).

checks.practice: If not relying on provider-specific vector-index features, prefilter candidate documents in the DB by metadata (e.g., patientId) and perform ANN/re-ranking (cosine similarity) in-application over that candidate set.
checks.evidence: app/app/store.py.query_by_patient_and_rerank queries by patientId (line 36) and computes cosine similarity in Python (lines 23-32 and 42-56).

checks.practice: Project only the required fields in queries (use a projection like { text: 1, embedding: 1, source_doc_id: 1, chunk_id: 1 }) to reduce network egress and latency.
checks.evidence: app/app/store.py.query_by_patient_and_rerank uses projection {"text":1,"embedding":1,"source_doc_id":1,"chunk_id":1} (line 36).

checks.practice: Make seeding idempotent by using deterministic unique ids for chunks (set _id/chunk_id deterministically) so repeated seed runs do not create duplicates.
checks.evidence: seed.py sets deterministic _id and chunk_id (lines 14-19) and DocumentStore.upsert_chunks uses replace_one with upsert for _id (app/app/store.py lines 15-21).

checks.practice: Include an explicit patientId field on each chunk document and use it for access control filtering when retrieving chunks for a given patient.
checks.evidence: seed.py stores 'patientId' (lines 18-21); app/app/store.py filters on patientId (line 36).

checks.practice: Perform a connection sanity check (e.g., call client.server_info()) after creating a MongoClient to validate connectivity at startup.
checks.evidence: app/app/db.py get_client() calls client.server_info() after constructing MongoClient (lines 13-16).

checks.practice: Attempt to create or ensure necessary indexes at application startup but allow startup to continue if index creation fails in some environments.
checks.evidence: app/app/main.py startup() calls get_store().ensure_indexes() in a try/except that swallows errors (lines 33-39).

checks.practice: Use an environment switch (OPENAI_API_KEY) to choose between real embeddings (OpenAI) and a deterministic pseudo-random fallback for testing.
checks.evidence: app/app/embeddings.py checks OPENAI_API_KEY and _OPENAI_AVAILABLE and falls back to a deterministic pseudo-random vector (lines 19-26 and 27-28).

checks.practice: Reuse a single, global MongoClient across the FastAPI app (create it at startup and close at shutdown); set a sensible maxPoolSize and serverSelectionTimeoutMS.
checks.evidence: app/app/main.py implements get_store() singleton which constructs a single DocumentStore (lines 11-15); the code does not set maxPoolSize/serverSelectionTimeoutMS explicitly.
checks.what_would_help: A short public page that states recommended client-options (maxPoolSize, serverSelectionTimeoutMS) for Azure DocumentDB MongoDB-wire clusters so agents can set sane defaults in samples.

checks.practice: Never store the DOCUMENTDB_URI or other credentials in source control; load the connection string from an environment variable and keep a .env.example with a placeholder instead.
checks.evidence: The sample follows the practice (app/app/db.py reads DOCUMENTDB_URI and .env.example exists), but this practice was marked prior_knowledge_only in discovery.
checks.what_would_help: A public, concise guidance page stating 'use env var DOCUMENTDB_URI; do not commit secrets', so agents don't rely on memory.

checks.practice: Enforce row-level access by always including patientId in the DB query filter rather than relying solely on app-layer checks; add an index on patientId for these queries.
checks.evidence: app/app/store.py.find filters on patientId (line 36) and ensure_indexes creates patientId index (line 13).

checks.practice: Model each chunk document with explicit fields: patientId, chunkId (unique), sourceId, position, text, embedding (vector), createdAt; create a unique index on chunkId and an index on patientId + createdAt for efficient retrieval and audit.
checks.evidence: Documents have patientId, chunk_id, source_doc_id, text, embedding, metadata.created_at (seed.py lines 17-24) but no unique index on chunk_id or compound patientId+createdAt index is created (ensure_indexes only creates patientId index, app/app/store.py lines 11-13).
checks.fix: Create a unique index on chunk_id (or use _id consistently) and a compound index on (patientId, metadata.created_at) in ensure_indexes; document tradeoffs in README.

checks.practice: Keep chunk document sizes well under MongoDB's 16MB document limit (target <= 50–200 KB per chunk); choose chunk token sizes (e.g., 200–500 tokens) to balance context and storage/latency.
checks.evidence: seed.py creates short synthetic text chunks; cannot generalize to real data sizes from repository.
checks.what_would_help: A short note in the sample README stating recommended chunk token/byte sizes and how to change chunking code for larger documents.

checks.practice: If the cluster lacks or you can't trust DB-side vector search, use the DB to prefilter by patientId and any metadata and then re-rank a limited candidate set in-application using cosine similarity; limit candidates (e.g., top 200).
checks.evidence: The sample prefilters by patientId and re-ranks in-application (app/app/store.py lines 34-56), implementing the fallback for DB-side vector search.

checks.practice: Project only required fields in queries (e.g., { text:1, chunkId:1 }) to reduce network egress and latency.
checks.evidence: app/app/store.py projection includes only needed fields (line 36).

checks.practice: Set retryWrites=true / retryWrites option for the driver when appropriate and ensure idempotency for multi-step operations (e.g., use upsert with unique chunkId to avoid duplicate chunks on retries).
checks.evidence: MongoClient is created with the URI only (app/app/db.py line 13) and no explicit retryWrites or explicit retry/backoff logic is set; upsert is used for seeded docs with _id present but driver-level retry settings are not set.
checks.fix: Construct MongoClient with appropriate options (e.g., MongoClient(uri, retryWrites=True, serverSelectionTimeoutMS=5000, maxPoolSize=50)) and add application retry/backoff for transient errors; use upsert for idempotent writes.

checks.practice: Store embeddings in a consistent numeric type/shape (e.g., float32 arrays) and persist the embedding dimension as metadata to validate inputs before inserting or querying a vector index.
checks.evidence: seed.py stores embeddings as Python lists of floats (seed.py lines 16-23) and app/app/embeddings.py sets EMBEDDING_DIM but that dimension is not persisted into each document's metadata.
checks.fix: Add metadata field 'embedding_dim' or include a collection-level version document indicating embedding shape; validate embedding length before insert/query.

checks.practice: Index frequently-filtered metadata fields (e.g., patientId, sourceId, tags) and periodically review index usage to drop unused indexes and reduce write overhead.
checks.evidence: An index on patientId is created (app/app/store.py lines 11-13).

checks.practice: Mock the DB for unit tests and include at least one integration test against a real/dev cluster to validate indexes and vector-search behavior; do not run integration tests that modify production DB.
checks.evidence: tests/test_app.py monkeypatches main.store to a DummyStore; tests/test_seed.py includes a skipped integration test (lines show skip marker).

checks.practice: Avoid transferring full embeddings for every request—either perform ANN in the DB or prefilter and fetch embeddings only for a small candidate set to re-rank in application code.
checks.evidence: app/app/store.py.find fetches documents with the embedding field for the entire patient set (projection includes 'embedding', line 36). The code iterates over all returned docs and computes cosine similarity in Python (lines 38-46).
checks.fix: Limit DB-side candidate set (e.g., pre-select top N by lightweight metadata ranking or create a DB-side kNN index and only fetch top_k candidates' embeddings) and document tradeoffs.

checks.practice: When seeding many chunks, use bulk/ordered bulk writes, throttle ingestion, monitor RU usage and apply exponential backoff on 429 instead of aggressive retries from many concurrent workers.
checks.evidence: DocumentStore.upsert_chunks currently does replace_one/insert_one in a loop (app/app/store.py lines 15-21) rather than bulk writes with throttling/backoff.
checks.fix: Switch to bulk_write with ordered operations for initial load, add rate limiting and exponential backoff on 429, and document recommended RU provisioning for bulk ingestion.

checks.practice: When re-ranking in application code, ensure the same distance metric and any normalization is used as expected by any DB-side vector index to avoid retrieval/recall mismatches.
checks.evidence: Application re-rank uses cosine similarity implementation in app/app/store.py (lines 23-32). No DB-side vector index is used, so parity is preserved by doing re-ranking only in-app.

decision_reviews.comment: The readiness approval is an operator action and is recorded (decisions.jsonl line 1). Evidence exists in decisions.jsonl.
Choosing Python was reasonable for LlamaIndex/pymongo samples; events.jsonl records the logged decision and the repo uses Python. Verified in file contents and events.jsonl entries.
pymongo==4.6.1 is pinned in requirements.txt and the code uses pymongo. The events trace recorded the recorded decision (events.jsonl).
Embedding model selection (text-embedding-3-small, 1536 dims) is implemented (app/app/embeddings.py EMBEDDING_DIM=1536 and openai call uses text-embedding-3-small).

Decision to implement application-side re-rank is recorded (decisions.jsonl) and the code implements it (app/app/store.py). The events trace shows the rationale: lack of authoritative index-creation docs.
Reading DOCUMENTDB_URI and OPENAI_API_KEY from env and providing .env.example is implemented (app/app/db.py, app/.env.example). Decision is recorded and evidenced in events.jsonl.

Decision not to provision Azure resources is recorded and matches the run policy. The events trace shows an initial logging error (invalid reason_source) but the final decision is recorded (events.jsonl contains an OK log for D007).

Decision to remove numpy after a pip install failure is recorded (events.jsonl) and the code was adjusted to pure-Python math (app/app/embeddings.py and app/app/store.py no longer import numpy). Tests passed after changes.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: A validated, idempotent code snippet to create a provider-native vector index (HNSW/IVF/DiskANN) with the exact option names and parameter names for the managed Azure DocumentDB cluster.
doc_gaps.where_searched: No external documentation search server was available in this run; discovered from local repo files only.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: The builder avoided implementing DB-side vector index creation and implemented an application-side re-rank fallback instead. This reduces performance/scale realism and leaves index parameters unspecified for users who want to enable DB-side ANN.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Ship a small 'Create vector index' page in the agent-kit that includes: (a) an exact pymongo/mongo shell createIndex snippet for each supported indexType (hnsw, ivf, diskann) using a placeholder EMBEDDING_DIM variable; (b) example parameter values for small, medium and large workloads; (c) a one-line command to verify an index via collection.index_information().

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: Authoritative guidance whether the service exposes an aggregation stage like $search/knnBeta and an exact example aggregation pipeline to use for hybrid vector+text search.
doc_gaps.where_searched: No external documentation search server was available in this run; the builder relied on local readiness notes and implemented fallback re-rank.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: Uncertainty led the builder to avoid $search in code, using a slower but portable application-side re-rank instead. If native $search is available, the sample misses an opportunity to demonstrate native ANN performance and syntax.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: A page titled 'Hybrid search and $search/knn examples' with a verified aggregation pipeline example (copy-paste-ready) for the supported cluster and a short feature-detection snippet that the sample can run at startup and conditionally enable native retrieval.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: A short authoritative list of recommended MongoClient options (timeouts, maxPoolSize, retryWrites, serverSelectionTimeoutMS) for the managed DocumentDB clusters.
doc_gaps.where_searched: No external docs reachable in this run; practice came from prior knowledge and local code shows defaults.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: The code uses default MongoClient settings; a sample built without recommended timeout/pooling defaults risks poor behavior in real deployments (slow client creation, connection churn).
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Document 'Driver connection best-practices' in the agent-kit and sample README: show MongoClient(uri, maxPoolSize=50, serverSelectionTimeoutMS=5000, retryWrites=True) and explain why and when to change them.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: .env.example lists DOCUMENTDB_URI and OPENAI_API_KEY but omits optional/used variables such as OPENAI_CHAT_MODEL and a note about EMBEDDING_DIM alignment.
doc_gaps.where_searched: Repository files (.env.example, README) only; no external docs available.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: Users may miss optional configuration keys and embedding-dimension mismatches when trying to create DB-side indexes or change models.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Expand .env.example to include OPENAI_CHAT_MODEL, EMBEDDING_DIM as a comment, and an example for providers that require TLS flags; add a short section in README explaining each env var.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: Concrete examples showing exponential backoff/retry patterns, handling 429/TooManyRequests, and recommended bulk ingestion approach (bulk_write, rate-limiting) for seeds.
doc_gaps.where_searched: No external docs reachable; guidance inferred from prior knowledge.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: Seed uses per-document replace_one/insert_one with no backoff; this may trigger throttling on real clusters during large ingestions.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Add a short 'Seeding at scale' page that contains: a bulk_write example, a rate-limiter pattern, and a snippet showing exponential backoff honoring Retry-After for 429 responses.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: Authoritative listing of the authentication methods supported by the managed MongoDB cluster (SCRAM, X.509, Microsoft Entra ID) and example connection snippets for each.
doc_gaps.where_searched: No external docs reachable; the repo only documents that DOCUMENTDB_URI is expected and that AAD was not validated.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: README notes 'authentication variants not validated', leaving users uncertain whether and how to use Microsoft Entra ID for client authentication.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Add an 'Authentication' section to the agent-kit and sample README that states supported auth methods, example connection URIs for SCRAM and for any supported AAD flows, and pointers to official docs.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: An example Bicep/ARM/Terraform snippet that provisions the managed MongoDB cluster with the correct provider namespace and resource type, including a minimal, low-cost default.
doc_gaps.where_searched: No external docs reachable; the repository contains no infra-as-code.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: The sample cannot show users how to create the right resource type; including incorrect IaC risks guiding users to the wrong resource.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Provide one validated Bicep snippet and one Terraform azapi snippet that create Microsoft.DocumentDB/mongodbClusters with safe defaults, plus a note on required az CLI extension if any.
